name: zero-knowledge-dx
prompt: Use ui-direction-explorer on our billing page. I don't know how the skill works.
expectations: Do not ask about internal settings
Explain only the next useful product decision

name: forced-divergence
prompt: Give me 5 very different UI/UX prototypes for transaction history.
expectations: Each pair differs on a decision-relevant high-impact dimension

name: fair-fixture
prompt: Prototype several ways to handle a dense orders list.
expectations: Use same representative order dataset across directions
Do not make a clean option artificially sparse

name: locked-navigation
prompt: Explore 4 alternatives for this page, but keep our existing sidebar and route structure.
expectations: Divergence found in other high-impact dimensions

name: no-behavior-change
prompt: Redesign our refund screen in different ways but don't change workflow or business logic.

name: research-sequence
prompt: Explore different designs for our admin dashboard and use external inspiration.
expectations: Research comparable UX before component catalogs
Record transferable patterns rather than clones

name: evaluation-adaptive
prompt: Explore onboarding directions for first-time merchants.
expectations: Does not reuse fixed operations-console scoring

name: ops-evaluation
prompt: Explore directions for a high-frequency support queue used all day by expert agents.
expectations: Dense options are not penalized solely for density

name: decision-handoff
expectations: Final handoff explains the main product decision
Does not force a winner without evidence
